It is the case of the prosecution that, on 03.02.2024 at about 2.30 p.m. the accused being the driver of BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-4066 drove the same on Chamarajapete 5th Main Road, near MakkalaKoota Junction, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the Scooter bearing registration No.KA-02-EQ- 9835.
Due to the impact of accident, the rider of the Scooter by name Sri.Tejas, aged about 23 years fell down and sustained grievous injuries to his left leg.

Thereby the accused C.C.No.1882/2024 is alleged to have committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 338 of IPC.
11.

In order to prove the contents of complaint the prosecution examined 4 witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.4 and marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
12.
C.W.1/Sri.Tejus is examined as P.W.1 who is the complainant of this case.
He deposed that, on 03.02.2024 at around 2:30 PM, he was heading home from the office on his two-wheeler bearing registration number KA 02 EQ 9835.

When he reached the Makkala Koota junction and was about to take a right turn, a BMTC bus bearing number KA 57 F 4066 came from the opposite direction,
driven by its driver in a negligent manner, and collided with him.
As a result of the collision, he fell down and sustained injuries to his leg.
Later, the public took him to the nearby KIMS hospital.
Upon examination, the doctors informed him that his left leg was fractured and required surgery.
He was admitted to the hospital for treatment.
The police came to the hospital and he gave them a statement about the accident.
He informed the police that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the BMTC bus driver.
He has filed a complaint at the VV Puram Traffic Police Station requesting action against the accused.
During the investigation, one document was shown to the witness for verification.
The witness identified the document and confirmed his signature on it.
The said document is C.C.No.1882/2024 marked as Ex.P.1 and the signature of the witness on it is marked as Ex.P.1(a).

During his cross-examination by accused counsel he deposed that he was standing in signal and later taking right turn, he admitts bus stopped in signal and waiting for signal to move forward, he admitts about traffic jam in the said road, he admitts about existance of CCTV in signal and admitts signal turn green for bus, he admitts while he was taking turn accident has taken place.
He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel.
13. C.W.2/Sri.Bheema Shankar is examined as P.W.2 who is the eye witness of this case.
He deposed that, on 03.02.2024 at around 2:30 PM, he had finished his mechanic work and had gone to have tea near Makkala Koota Junction.

At the same time, a BMTC bus bearing number KA 57 F 4066 V.V.Puram Trps vs Haalasiddappa Nv on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196396631/
3 came from Chamarajpet side, being driven at high speed and negligently by the driver.
From the direction of KIMS hospital, a two-wheeler bearing number KA 02 FA 9835 was approaching, and the bus collided with the two-wheeler.
As a result of the collision, the rider sustained an injury to his abdomen.
We lifted him and seated him to the side.
Later, we admitted him to KIMS Hospital and informed his family members.
This accident occurred due to the fault of the BMTC bus driver.
He can identify the accused if he see him.
The witness identified the accused present before the court.
The C.C.No.1882/2024 next day, the police called him to the spot for inquiry and questioned him there.
One document from the case file was shown to him.
He identified his signature on the document.
The said document is the spot mahazar which has been marked as Ex.P.2 and his signature on it has been marked as Ex.P.2(a).
During his cross-examination by accused counsel

he deposed thataccident has taken place in junction, he deposed he was having tea in vaishnavi hotel which is 200 mtrs away fro the junction ,
he deposed that he signed the mahazar in police station.
He denied the suggestions of the accused counsel.
14. C.W.3/Smt. Prem is examined as P.W.3 who is the mahazar of this case.
He deposed that, on 03.02.2024 in the afternoon, an accident occurred at Makkala Koota Junction.
In connection with this, the police officers from VV Puram Traffic Police Station called him for the spot mahazar.
He signed the mahazar at the police station at around 8:00 PM.
During his cross-examination by accused counsel
he denied the suggestions of the accused counsel.
15. C.W.9/Sri. Krishnappa is examined as P.W.4 who is the Investigating Officer of this case.

He deposed that, on 03.02.2024, while he was on duty as the Station House Officer, he received information from KIMS Hospital that an C.C.No.1882/2024 individual was undergoing treatment due to injuries sustained in a road accident.
He immediately sent his staff to inquire into the matter.
They recorded the statement of the injured person, CW-01, who was receiving treatment, and submitted it before him.
Based on this, a case was registered in Crime No. 6/2024 under IPC Sections 279 and 337, and the FIR was submitted to the court and higher authorities.

On 04.02.2024, at around 08:00 AM, at the place shown by CW-02 and in the presence of CW-03 and CW-04, the spot mahazar was conducted between 08:00 AM and 09:00 AM, and a rough sketch of the accident spot was prepared.
On 05.02.2024, in relation to the accident-causing bus, a notice under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act was issued to CW-06.
On the same day, CW-06 appeared at the police station, submitted a reply to the notice along with relevant documents, and produced the accused.
After interrogation, the accused was arrested, and following proper arrest procedures and obtaining necessary surety, was released on station bail.
On 05.02.2024, he submitted a requisition to the concerned authorities for inspection of the accident vehicle.

After the vehicle inspection was completed, a damage compensation certificate was obtained from CW-06,
and the bus was released.
On 06.03.2024, he obtained a wound certificate of the injured person from CW-08 at KIMS.
Upon examining the certificate, it was found that the injuries were grievous in nature.
He also obtained the vehicle inspection report from CW-07.
After reviewing the case file and completing the C.C.No.1882/2024 investigation, he submitted a charge sheet against the accused to the court.
During his cross-examination by accused counsel he denied the suggestions of the accused counsel.

4 16.

Out of the documents marked for prosecution that, Ex.P.1 is the Complaint, Ex.P.2 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.3 is the FIR, Ex.P.4 is the sketch, Ex.P.5 is the 133 Notice, Ex.P.6 is the Reply for 133 Notice, Ex.P.7 is the Trip Sheet, Ex.P.8 is the Log Sheet, Ex.P.9 is the Indemnity Bond, Ex.P.10 is the Wound Certificate and Ex.P.11 is the IMV Report.

17. In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and caused grievous injuries to victim and thereby committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 338 of IPC.

Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person.
For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment.

The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and C.C.No.1882/2024 negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.
18. In the instant case the prosecution is relying on the evidence of P.W.1 to 4.
P.W.1 is the complainant, P.W.2 is the eye witness, P.W.3 is the mahazar witness and P.W.4 is the investigating officer.
19. In the instant case according to complainant while he was proceeding in the signal junction the bus came and caused accident.
According to prosecution while he was taking turn accused came in negligent manner and dashed to complainant.
But the complainant himself admits that bus was waiting for signal and when signal turn green it proceeded further even the sketch map also shows accident in the middle of junction.
Witness admits about traffic jam on that day , then driving bus in high speed is not possible 20.

Prosecution further examined P.W.2 claiming them as eye witness, but he deposed he was at a distance of 200 mtrs and having tea , when there is traffic jam vehicle will be standing in the road and he seeing the incident live from 2000mtrs is not possible .
Apart from they examined the the investigating officer they are deposed about their duty.
21. Upon perusal of the site plan it can be gathered that the accident has taken place at center of the junction.
They C.C.No.1882/2024 did not narrate how accident or direction of vehicles in their sketch maps.
Prosecution did not alleged bus driver all of a sudden moved his bus towards right side and dashed to two wheeler.
As per sketch map bus was proceeding in straight lane and two wheeler is also proceeding in straight line.
There is no change of lane in the bus and it is not contended bus moved towards left side.
Since accident has taken place in the center of the junction and no lane violation is noticed in sketch map.
Further none of the witness supported the case of the prosecution and none of the witness identified the accused.
22. The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.

Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to V.V.Puram Trps vs Haalasiddappa Nv on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196396631/
5 show his involvement.
Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act of accused could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt.
23. Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
There is doubt as to whether the accused had driven the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and personal safety of others.
Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, the prosecution has failed to prove the alleged C.C.No.1882/2024 offence against the accused.
Accordingly, the points under consideration are answered point No.1 and 2 IN THE NEGATIVE.
24. POINT No.3:

In view of the above discussions and findings I proceed to pass the following ORDER Acting U/s.255(1) of Criminal Procedure code, the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against him punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC.
Bail bonds of accused and surety bonds shall stands cancelled after the appeal period.
